sensors.name: line tracker, brightness of the floor in % (LINETRACKER)

actions.name: curve forward, left wheel 7 %, right wheel 22 % (curves left)
curve forward, left wheel 22 %, right wheel 7 % (curves right)

control_flow: In followLine: if the line tracker reads below 30 %, curve left; else if it reads above 70 %, curve right; else drive straight on.

decision_points.condition: first: the line tracker's brightness is below 30 % (black); second: it is above 70 % (the white band or the peach floor)

branches.outcome: not below 30 %, but above 70 %: it curves right

branches.reason: Readings that are neither black (0 %) nor white/peach (83 % to 100 %) happen only for an instant right at the edge of the black core, so no world holds this value still.
branches.outcome: between 30 % and 70 %: it drives straight on

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left while it sees black, curves right while it sees white, and would drive straight on in between
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light, facing along it
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker goes from black to the white band and back, again and again
scenarios.title: Follows the line to its end
assumptions: The end of the line is where it should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end

uncertainties: You don't say where the line ends or what the robot should do there, so the test takes the line's end as the goal.
Above 70 % is also the plain peach floor (about 83 %): off the line the robot curves right without end, so a test needs a line under it from the start.
Readings between 30 % and 70 % last only an instant at the edge of the black core, so the straight-ahead part can't be tested on its own.
